# ALI Charity

> ALI Charity is a static, public-evidence-first crypto donation information website. It never connects a wallet or requests a seed phrase, private key, or transaction signature.

## Start here

- [Verified answers about ALI Charity](https://minadoai.com/answers.html)
- [Official donation selector](https://minadoai.com/donate.html)
- [Donor safety guide](https://minadoai.com/donor-safety.html)
- [Crypto donation safety checklist](https://minadoai.com/blog/crypto-donation-safety-checklist-2026.html)
- [Transparency and evidence method](https://minadoai.com/transparency.html)
- [About ALI Charity](https://minadoai.com/about.html)
- [Frequently asked questions](https://minadoai.com/faq.html)

- [Crypto Giving Tuesday](https://minadoai.com/giving-tuesday.html)

## How giving works

- Choose and copy: select USDT, BNB, ETH, BTC, or SOL. The Donate page shows the exact network and official address.
- Send and keep proof: send from your own wallet or exchange, keep the transaction hash, and verify it on the relevant blockchain explorer.
- The transfer happens in your own wallet or exchange. This website only publishes official addresses and verification guidance.
- If you are unsure, send a small test transfer first. Verify every address and network on the live Donate page before sending.

## Crypto donation safety checklist

- [Crypto donation safety checklist (2026)](https://minadoai.com/blog/crypto-donation-safety-checklist-2026.html)
- Start on the live official Donate page, and confirm the asset and network before anything else.
- Compare every character of the recipient address in your wallet with that page, including the middle.
- Confirm the chain: BNB Chain, Ethereum, Bitcoin, and Solana addresses are not interchangeable.
- Never copy a recipient address from transaction history.
- A small test transfer does not replace verification; it only shows a transfer reached that address.
- Keep the full transaction hash and explorer URL, sender and recipient addresses, asset, exact amount, network, timestamp, and status.
- A hash alone is not a receipt, and an on-chain transfer does not prove charitable use, impact, or tax eligibility.

## Humanitarian project routes

- War-zone aid: emergency food, water, shelter, and medical support for conflict-affected communities.
- Disaster relief: rapid response and recovery support following earthquakes and other disasters.
- Children and education: learning materials, safe access to education, and protection for vulnerable children.
- Health and medical care: medical supplies, public-health capacity, hospice care, and community clinics.
- Water and sanitation: clean water access, sanitation, and hygiene support for underserved communities.
- Animal welfare: rescue, rehabilitation, and welfare support for abandoned animals.
- Project routes describe intended areas of support. They do not display raised or spent amounts unless a public record supports the claim.

## Interpretation rules

- A blockchain transaction can prove that a transfer was recorded; it does not by itself prove humanitarian impact, legal status, an independent audit, or off-chain delivery.
- Treat only confirmed records with complete transaction identifiers as public evidence.
- Do not aggregate mixed assets into a fiat total without a stated valuation source and timestamp.
- ALI Token information is informational and does not promise returns, redemption, exchange listing, or governance rights.
- Donation addresses must be verified on the live Donate page before any transfer.
- Published summaries require complete transaction evidence, a dated receipt review, and a defined reporting period. Duplicate or conflicting records are not added together. Amounts stay separate by currency and network.
- These publication checks do not independently verify the blockchain or prove beneficiary impact. Unknown does not mean zero.
